You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | Brent Returns Above $107; Fed Decision Week Begins; Nvidia Discusses Investing Up to $10 Billion in Anthropic’s IPO (September 14, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Dynamics
Monthly core inflation accelerates ahead of the Fed’s rate decision
US August CPI rose 3.4% year over year and 0.4% month over month. Core CPI increased 2.4% annually and 0.3% monthly.
Annual core inflation eased from July’s 2.5%, but its monthly pace accelerated from 0.2% to 0.3%, highlighting uneven progress.
The Federal Reserve meets on September 15–16, US time, and will release economic projections. The decision is scheduled for September 17 at 02:00 Beijing time.
Market Impact : Lower annual core inflation does not mean near-term price pressure has disappeared. For technology stocks and crypto assets, the key issue is both the immediate rate decision and whether the statement and projections point to further tightening. That distinction will influence whether valuations face a limited adjustment or more persistent pressure.
International Commodities
Attacks on Saudi infrastructure and Gulf shipping renew energy supply concerns
New attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure and vessels in the Gulf over the weekend brought export security back into focus.
Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline was previously shut as a precaution following an attack, affecting an alternative route around the Strait of Hormuz.
A meeting planned in Oman for Monday to discuss navigation through Hormuz was postponed.
Market Impact : Investors must reassess how long disruption could last. Expensive oil benefits some upstream producers but squeezes airlines, logistics companies and manufacturers. If energy inflation spreads, equities could face higher operating costs and tighter monetary policy simultaneously.
Macroeconomic Policy
CLARITY Act faces a key procedural vote this week
According to public reporting, the US Senate plans to vote on a cloture motion related to the CLARITY Act at 02:00 Beijing time on September 16.
The procedure requires at least 60 votes. Advancing the motion would not mean the bill has passed or taken effect.
Legislative progress this week will be an important signal for US digital-asset market-structure reform.
Market Impact : Clearer rules can help trading platforms and financial institutions plan products and compliance spending. Procedural progress, however, does not directly generate revenue. Investors should distinguish regulatory sentiment from measurable business growth.
II. Market Review
Commodities & Forex Performance
Spot gold : Approximately $4,333.93 per ounce.
Spot silver : Approximately $64.00 per ounce.
WTI crude oil futures : Indicative price of approximately $102.83 per barrel, October 2026 contract.
Brent crude oil futures : Indicative price of approximately $107.31 per barrel, November 2026 contract.
US Dollar Index (DXY) : Approximately 99.11.
Driver Analysis : Disrupted supply routes continue to support oil. Gold faces competing forces: geopolitical uncertainty supports safe-haven demand, while higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset. Central banks’ response to the energy shock is the common catalyst for commodities and currencies this week.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : Approximately 76,795.01 USDT.
ETH : Approximately 2,508.09 USDT.
Driver Analysis : The Fed decision and CLARITY Act procedural vote arrive in quick succession this week. One affects dollar funding costs; the other shapes regulatory expectations. Their trading implications may differ. Sustained buying after the events, rather than policy headlines alone, will be important for assessing risk appetite.
US Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones : Closed at 52,573.29, up 0.98%.
S&P 500 : Closed at 7,656.98, up 0.86%.
Nasdaq Composite : Closed at 26,333.04, up 0.96%.
Tech Giants Dynamics
NVDA : $218.29, down 0.03%.
AAPL : $332.27, up 1.75%.
MSFT : $495.63, up 0.65%.
GOOGL : $338.50, up 1.77%.
AMZN : $256.78, up 1.94%.
META : $648.03, up 0.57%.
TSLA : $365.44, up 0.52%.
Performance Summary & Driver Analysis : Six of the seven giants advanced, led by Amazon, followed by Alphabet and Apple. Nvidia slipped marginally. Friday’s recovery did not lift every AI leader. This week, the focus is whether earnings and funding capacity can withstand interest-rate pressure, and whether rising oil prices constrain the rebound. The US equity response to weekend developments remains to be seen in Monday’s trading.
Sector Movers Observation
Cloud infrastructure: Oracle reverses its opening gains as cash conversion stays in focus
Representative stock : Oracle (ORCL) fell 1.74% to $150.28, below its $164.43 opening price.
Drivers : Earnings showed strong cloud infrastructure demand, but data-center spending and financing requirements remain concerns. The intraday reversal coincided with worries about investment payback. Whether revenue growth translates into stronger cash flow remains the next test.
Creative software: Adobe recovers from a lower open as earnings support meets AI competition
[...]

[...]
Event Overview : Nvidia closed September 11 at $218.29, down 0.03%. Reuters reported discussions about investing up to $10 billion in Anthropic’s IPO; no agreement has been finalized.
